Subject: Access controls & data residency - follow-up

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

What we covered
- Overview: how Redwood serves inference (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and tradeoffs for data residency.
- Your priorities: strict PII handling, configurable retention, full audit logging for support access, RBAC/least-privilege controls, and a documented break-glass emergency flow.

Open items you asked for (next steps)
1) Short answers & attachments summarizing our controls (SOC 2 scope, RBAC, support process) — attached.
2) Confirm per-tenant data residency options and recommended deployment mode for Databank.
3) Break-glass process details and audit trail examples.
4) Proposed follow-up: 30-min technical Q&A with our infra/security lead (Dev Patel) — please send 2 available times.

Immediate answers (short):
- PII: Redwood can restrict which model prompt/response data is persisted; customers can opt-in to retention. For regulated workloads we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated with customer-managed keys.
- Data residency: Dedicated/Private can be pinned to a cloud region or on-prem; hosted customers can be routed to nearest region by policy (enterprise customers can request regional pinning).
- Logging/support access: Support access is gated by RBAC and requires just-in-time elevation with MFA; all session activity is logged and exported to audit logs.
- Break-glass: emergency access requires an approval flow (security + customer point-of-contact), and all activity during the break-glass session is immutable and stored in audit logs.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf (summary), access_controls_matrix.xlsx (roles, privileges, and examples).

Can you confirm which items you want us to expand into a short package for Legal / InfoSec? If you share two times for next week I’ll loop Dev.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Thanks Sanjay — answers inline and next steps below.

1) Residency
- Hosted: routing-by-region is standard; strict hard pinning (all storage + logs remain in a single region) is available for enterprise customers but requires Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Redwood Private. For Databank’s compliance profile I recommend Dedicated in us-east-1 or Redwood Private (VPC) if you need customer-managed networking and KMS.

2) Deletion requests
- We provide a deletion SLA for retained prompt/log data for Dedicated/Private customers: standard turnaround is 7 business days; expedited 48 hours can be added to enterprise contracts. We provide a deletion certificate (audit record) once complete. Hosted customers have different retention policies — we can attach the hosted retention matrix if needed.

3) Support access
- Access model: RBAC with least-privilege roles. Support sessions use just-in-time (JIT) elevation via an approved workflow; access windows are time-boxed, MFA enforced. All session activity is logged (who accessed what, commands, timestamps) and the logs are immutable. You can specify a named list of support principals for Dedicated/Private and we’ll restrict break-glass to that list by contract.

4) Break-glass
- Process: customer notifies account + security OR Redwood detects critical incident -> security triage -> break-glass approval (customer can require secondary approver). During break-glass all actions are recorded and a post-action audit report is provided.

Attachments & artifacts
- Re-attached: Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf, access_controls_matrix.xlsx (includes role examples and recommended bindings).
- I’ve added links to our compliance pack and a short diagram showing the break-glass flow: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-access-controls

Next steps
- Confirm which artifacts you want sent to Legal (SOC2 summary, full SOC 2 report, retention matrix, access matrix).
- I’ll schedule the 30-min tech Q&A; Dev (cc’d) will cover RBAC, audit logs, and break-glass implementation. Tue 8/31 10:00am PT works for us — I’ll send a calendar invite.
